name: SearXNG
use_label: Search engine that doesn't track you
one_liner: A free metasearch engine that neither tracks nor profiles you, aggregating up to 261 search services.

text.why: Every search leaves a trail that feeds ads and recommendations. SearXNG asks many search services on your behalf, returns only the results, and says users are neither tracked nor profiled.
text.take: You can try one of the public instances listed at searx.space right away.
build: The documentation lists up to 261 search engines, optional JavaScript and cookies, use over Tor, 58 translations, and self-hosting on your own server.

who.role: People who don't want a search history, and admins who want to run their own search service.

start.text: Use a public instance from searx.space, or follow the Installation guide in the documentation to set up your own.

caveat: Licensed AGPL-3.0: if you offer a modified version as a network service you must share the source. Public instances are run by different people, so how far to trust one is your call.

license.scope_text: Release source if you redistribute or host it as a service.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: The SearXNG documentation home page: 'Welcome to SearXNG', 'Search without being tracked', and a features list.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
null in the JSON means not observed — never zero. The Markdown writes [unconfirmed] for it.
